strategy_objective_guidance:
- Single scored quantity: `combined_score = (dmin/dmax)^2 / (1/4.165849767)`, i.e. the squared ratio of smallest to largest pairwise distance, rescaled so 1.0 matches the reference ratio. No cap, no other terms, no time penalty (only a wall-clock timeout).
- Hard validity constraints: return a NumPy-compatible array of shape (14, 3), finite values, at least two distinct points so dmax > 0 (otherwise score 0). Any exception → score 0, so robustness matters more than marginal gains.
- The objective is scale/translation/rotation invariant, so normalization is purely an optimization convenience. A canonical formulation: maximize t s.t. d(i,j)^2 ≥ t and d(i,j)^2 ≤ 1 for all pairs — a smooth constrained NLP with 91 pairwise constraints.
- No term rewards anything other than the nominal goal (best-packing-like spread of 14 points); the weighting does not distort the problem. The largest lever is simply raising dmin/dmax beyond the reference ~0.4905 (squared), i.e. finding a better 14-point spherical/euclidean spread than the baseline.
- Input is fully known offline (n=14, d=3 fixed); no streaming/causality concerns. Batch, global, and expensive offline optimization are all permitted within the timeout.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Symmetric polyhedral constructions: place points at vertices of highly symmetric solids (icosahedron + cube, rhombicuboctahedron variants, antiprism + cap points), then optimize within the symmetry family; pure NumPy construction plus small parametric search. Mechanism: symmetric point sets often have near-optimal min/max distance ratios; a 2–6 parameter family is cheap to grid-search deterministically.
- Direct constrained NLP on the squared-distance formulation: `scipy.optimize.minimize` with SLSQP or trust-constr, maximizing t with constraints d²ij ≥ t, d²ij ≤ 1 (91 constraints, 43 variables). Mechanism: directly optimizes the exact scored quantity with its gradient; trust-constr handles the constraint Jacobian well.
- Unconstrained smooth-surrogate optimization: minimize a soft objective like logsumexp of −d²ij plus penalty on max distance (e.g. penalty on d²ij exceeding a cap), using `scipy.optimize.minimize` (L-BFGS-B / BFGS) with analytic gradients. Mechanism: smooth min/max surrogates avoid the nonsmoothness of min/max of 91 distances.
- Global stochastic multistart: many random or quasi-random (`scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol`) initializations on the unit sphere, each polished by local optimization, keep best. Mechanism: landscape is highly multimodal (many local optima differing in symmetry class); deterministic multistart with fixed seed is the reliable way to escape bad basins.
- Nonconvex-global heuristics: differential evolution (`scipy.optimize.differential_evolution`) on a reduced/symmetry-parameterized model, or simulated annealing on a soft-min objective. Mechanism: global search over the few symmetry parameters; keep the full 42-dim space to local polishers.
- Repulsion/force-based relaxation: iterative gradient ascent on a potential Σ 1/d²ij (or log-barrier pushing points apart) with projection onto a bounding sphere, then rescale. Mechanism: classic spherical-spread relaxation, cheap and robust; good initializer generator for the NLP families above.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Active-set refinement: after local optimization, identify the pairs attaining dmin and dmax; reoptimize with only those constraints active, using trust-constr with tight tolerances (gtol ~1e-10) — the optimum is determined by the active contact graph.
- Multistart budget tuning: scale number of starts (e.g. 32 → 256) with a fixed seed (`np.random.default_rng(0)`), each with a modest iteration cap, then deep-polish only the top few candidates with high-precision SLSQP/trust-constr.
- Symmetry-preserving polish: parameterize candidate solutions by orbit structure under a point group (e.g. two parallel regular heptagons, antiprism + axis points) and optimize the few remaining parameters to machine precision — symmetric families often contain configurations at or beyond the reference ratio.
- Smooth-min annealing: gradually sharpen the softmin (logsumexp temperature 1 → 1e-6) across successive optimization stages, so the surrogate converges to the true min; pair with a shrinking penalty on dmax exceeding the cap.
- Robustness/fallback: wrap all optimization in try/except; always compare against a hard-coded-in-code (not evaluator-derived) symmetric incumbent and return whichever scores higher; validate shape, finiteness, and dmax > 0 before returning. Verify the final array with `scipy.spatial.distance.pdist` internally to guarantee the returned configuration matches the intended score.

strategies.title: [epigraph-nlp] Exact epigraph NLP with trust-constr on all 91 pairwise constrain
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: epigraph-constrained NLP (direct exact-ratio formulation)
Replacement scope: Replace the entire `obj`/L-BFGS surrogate loop inside `min_max_dist_dim3_14` (the objective, the optimizer, and the start-polishing phase), keeping the multistart loop skeleton and the exact_ratio incumbent tracking.
Compute budget: ≤ 40 starts, ≤ 400 trust-constr iterations each (gtol 1e-9); expected wall time ~15–25 s, well within timeout. Deterministic seed 0.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent optimizes a soft-min/soft-max surrogate at fixed temperature β=200; at finite β the surrogate optimum is biased away from the true ratio optimum, and dmax is only weakly controlled. The epigraph form maximizes the exact scored quantity: variables (x_1..x_14 ∈ R³, t), maximize t subject to ||x_i − x_j||² ≥ t for all 91 pairs and ||x_i − x_j||² ≤ 1 for all pairs (the ≤1 constraints fix scale). This removes the surrogate bias entirely — the incumbent's returned ratio 0.4720 (squared 0.22274) is a surrogate-biased local point, and the exact NLP with analytic constraint Jacobians converges to the true KKT point of the same basin, which strictly exceeds it because the surrogate's optimum is not the ratio's optimum.
Plan: variables z = (P.ravel(), t), 43 dims. Objective f = −t, gradient [0…0, −1]. Constraints: 91 lower bounds g_k = d²_k − t ≥ 0 and 91 upper bounds h_k = 1 − d²_k ≥ 0, with analytic Jacobians (rows: 2(x_i−x_j) in the coordinate slots, −1 in t slot; −2(x_i−x_j)). Use `scipy.optimize.minimize(..., method="trust-constr")` with `NonlinearConstraint` and supplied jacobians. Starts: the incumbent's best configuration (rescaled so dmax=1, t initialized at dmin²), the heptagonal antiprism, and ~35 seeded random sphere configurations rescaled to dmax=1. Track exact ratio after each solve; return best. Wrap each start in try/except; fall back to the best incumbent found (never return invalid data). Validity: output is the optimizer's point array, shape (14,3), finite by construction (check finiteness and dmax>0 before return).
Expected-gain check: the incumbent's own basin, re-solved exactly, must yield squared ratio strictly above the surrogate-biased 0.22274 (predicted combined_score > 0.9279, plausibly ≥ 1.0 since the reference squared ratio 1/4.1658 ≈ 0.2400 is achievable in symmetric basins); falsifiable threshold: combined_score ≥ 0.95.

strategies.title: [orbit-family] Two-poles + two staggered hexagonal rings parametric family with
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: point-group orbit parameterization (subsystem replacement of the search space)
Replacement scope: Replace the 42-dimensional spherical-coordinate search with a 5-parameter symmetric family search plus a symmetry-preserving polish; the incumbent's random multistart phase is discarded, the incumbent best is kept only as fallback comparison.
Compute budget: differential evolution over 5 parameters with popsize 20, maxiter 200, seed fixed (≤ ~4000 objective evaluations, each a closed-form construction + pdist, ~2 s), plus ≤ 10 trust-constr polishes at ≤ 300 iterations; total well under timeout.
Gain mechanism: The best-known 14-point configurations in R³ for min/max distance have layered symmetry (e.g. 2 antipodal axis points + two staggered hexagons, or heptagonal-antiprism-like classes); the incumbent's unconstrained 42-dim search wastes dimension exploring symmetry-broken basins. The new degree of freedom the incumbent lacks: variable ring radius and latitude per ring and independent twist, allowing the two hexagons to sit off the unit sphere at different radii — the free-space optimum is not on a sphere, and the sphere constraint in the incumbent is a genuine restriction, not just a normalization.
Plan: family P(θ): poles at (0,0,±h); ring 1: 6 points at z = z1, radius r1, angles 2πk/6; ring 2: 6 points at z = z2, radius r2, angles 2πk/6 + α. Parameters θ = (h, z1, r1, z2, r2, α) (6 params, α bounded [0, π/6] by symmetry). Objective: exact dmin/dmax via pdist. Run `differential_evolution` with bounds h∈[0.1,2], z1,z2∈[−1,1], r1,r2∈[0.1,2], α∈[0,π/6], tol 1e-10, polish=True, seed 7. Then take the top 3 distinct θ and polish each with the epigraph NLP of Strategy 1 restricted to a small trust region (or full-space trust-constr warm start) to escape the family boundary. Return best exact ratio among family optimum, polished optima, and the incumbent fallback. Validity: closed-form finite coordinates; check shape/finiteness/dmax>0 before return.
Expected-gain check: the off-sphere radii r1 ≠ r2 and variable h are degrees of freedom the sphere-constrained incumbent structurally cannot realize, so the family's exact-ratio optimum is not comparable to the incumbent's constrained basin; falsifiable threshold: combined_score ≥ 0.95, with the known layered-symmetric constructions expected to reach squared ratio ≥ 0.24 (score ≥ 1.0).

strategies.title: [repulsion-relax] Inverse-square repulsion with dmax cap projection as basin gen
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: force-directed relaxation (distinct escape direction for basin generation)
Replacement scope: Replace the random-start generator inside the multistart loop (the 24 uniform spherical starts) with repulsion-relaxation trajectories; keep the incumbent's L-BFGS surrogate polisher and incumbent tracking intact.
Compute budget: ≤ 30 relaxation runs, each ≤ 2000 gradient steps with adaptive step (vectorized, ~1 s total), then ≤ 30 L-BFGS polishes at the existing 500-iteration cap; total ≈ incumbent's runtime, ~10–15 s.
Gain mechanism: Uniform random starts land in low-quality asymmetric basins; the incumbent's multistart is effectively sampling the same mediocre attractors. A projected inverse-square repulsion flow Σ_ij ∇(1/d²_ij) with a hard cap on dmax (radial rescale to dmax = 1 every step, i.e. relaxation inside the diameter-1 ball rather than on the sphere) drives configurations toward equalized contact graphs — a different escape direction that lands in distinct symmetry classes (e.g. icosahedron-plus-poles-like topologies) the uniform sphere sampler almost never reaches. The new degree of freedom: points may leave the sphere surface during relaxation, since the scored objective only constrains the diameter, not a sphere.
Plan: initialize 30 runs with seeded rng (seed 123) uniform in the unit ball (not on the sphere). Each step: compute repulsive forces F_i = Σ_j 2(x_i − x_j)/d_ij⁴, take adaptive step (backtracking if any d² drops below a barrier floor), then rescale all points so dmax = 1. After each run, feed the result into the existing `obj`/L-BFGS polisher (with its incumbent comparison). Also include 3 structured starts: icosahedron vertices (12) + 2 antipodal points along an unused axis, and a cuboctahedron + 8 face-cap points, all relaxed by the same flow. Keep the heptagonal-antiprism start and the best-incumbent fallback. Validity: every candidate passes through the same exact-ratio check; return best finite (14,3) array with dmax>0.
Expected-gain check: the diameter-ball (not sphere) relaxation and the structured icosahedral/cuboctahedral seeds are contact topologies the incumbent's spherical uniform sampler cannot generate, so its best basin (squared ratio 0.22274) is not the reachable set here; falsifiable threshold: combined_score ≥ 0.93 from at least one new topology, with upside toward ≥ 1.0 if the icosahedral class contains the reference-ratio configuration.
